Keyboard shortcuts

  • ? show or hide this list
  • P pause or resume time
  • 1 2 3 4 camera: overview, close-up, aerial, isometric

Shortcuts pause while you are typing in a text box. You can change the keys in Settings.

Challenge runs

A challenge run is a set number of seasons from a fixed start. You are scored on how well the settlement is run and how far it grows, and compared with a par: what a plain autopilot scores from the same start. It needs a fresh settlement (before the first season).

Time-lapse

Scrub back through this settlement as the civic map, one frame per season you played (the last 120 seasons are kept). The 3D scene cannot be rebuilt for a past season, so this is the 2D map, and you can download an image strip of it.

Solid line: sustainability. Dashed line: people. ◆ era   ▲ discovery   ■ first of a building   ● founder's note.

Pinned moments

Advisor council

Four invented advisors, each caring about one corner of the settlement, disagree on what to do this season. Every recommendation is checked by running the coming season twice on a copy: once taken, once not. Their trust and record are scored against what really would have happened, whether or not you took the advice. They are fictional characters; the numbers are your settlement's own.

How past advice turned out

Dynasty

Every settlement you play can bank Legacy points when it ends (you found a new one, it collapses, or you press the button). Points buy permanent perks below. Perks rest during a challenge run or consulting case so those stay comparable, and you can switch them off.

Banners and skyline flourishes

Cosmetic only. Unlocked by achievements and Dynasty rank, shown in the archive and on the shareable card.

Era doctrines

When the settlement enters a new era you may adopt one doctrine for it. A doctrine makes some research branches cheaper and adds one small standing bonus. Each kind counts once; adopting the same kind in a second era makes it half again as strong. (The Dynasty perk Schools of Thought deepens the discounts.) Choices are written into the Founder's Log.

Doctrines so far

Notable citizens

Invented people, not real ones. A child appears in every era, is apprenticed in the next and becomes a master of that era's trade in the one after, giving a small standing bonus (shown in City Views). You can switch the whole feature off.

        Consulting mode (optional, harder)
        
Instead of founding a settlement, take over a city that is already in trouble and turn it around: hold a Steady or better score for three seasons in a row within thirty seasons. Only offered before you play a season; you can abandon the case for a fresh start.

    Tribal era
    
      
    Season 1
    
      
      
    Founded Year 1
    
      
    People: 6
    
      
    Shelter for 8
    
      
    i
    Population only grows when there's shelter room to spare and the settlement has a full season of food surplus banked. "Overcrowded" halts growth completely until more shelter is built, even if food is otherwise fine.
    
      
    Food: 20 / 30
    
      
    i
    The number after the slash is a hard ceiling, not just a target — any food gathered beyond what storage can hold spoils and is lost at the end of the season. Storage pits raise that ceiling.
    
      
    Materials: 20
    
      
    Tools: 2.0
    
      
    Knowledge: 0.0
    
      
    Surplus: 0.0
    
      
      
    Output per person: -
    
      
    Time played: 0 min
    
      
    Calm seasons in a row: 0
    
      
    Land health: 100%
    
      
    i
    The land can only give so much per season. Harvesting more than that sustainable amount degrades land health, which cuts every future harvest — staying under the line lets it recover instead. This is what lets a small, careful settlement out-score a big, careless one.
    
      
    
      
    
      
    The settlement is waiting on your word.
    
    
    

    
    
      
    Sustainability
    
      
    Sustainability: 0 / 100
    
      
    i
    Every input to this score is a ratio — food per person, shelter per person — never a raw count, so growing the settlement without growing what it needs to support that size won't raise it. It's the average of the four equally-weighted components below.
    
      
    
      
    
        
    Livability: 0
    
        
    Equity: 0
    
        
    Resource balance: 0
    
        
    Resilience: 0
    
      
    
      
    i
    Equity isn't an average of your three basic provisions (food, shelter, gathering space) — it's capped by whichever one is met worst, and docked further when provision is lopsided. Grand shelters don't help this number if people are still going hungry.
    
      
    A settlement that grows isn't automatically a settlement worth living in.

    One tree, sixteen tiers, eight eras. What you lean into now changes what opens later.
        
    i
    A tier only opens once two nodes in the tier below it are researched — you don't need everything in a tier, just enough to prove the ground beneath it. Some nodes also require a minimum number of discoveries already made in one branch, so leaning into a branch early can open or close doors many tiers later.
